newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Central Americans prepare Clinton visit agenda.
newsitem.headline: Central Americans prepare Clinton visit agenda.

text.p: Central American foreign ministers said on Tuesday they had fine-tuned a declaration focusing on trade and immigration that the region's presidents will sign when they meet with President Bill Clinton on May 8 in Costa Rica.
The ministers said those two issues will take center stage when the presidents meet with Clinton in San Jose during the U.S. leader's first official visit to Latin America.

"The Central American presidents will propose that we move toward closer economic relations with the United States and I interpret that the United States looks very positively upon the Central American position," Costa Rican Foreign Minister Fernando Naranjo told reporters.

Naranjo said he came to Guatemala from a trip to Washington D.C., where he met with U.S. State Department officials to get their reaction to elements of a rough draft of the declaration that Clinton and the Central American presidents will sign.
According to Naranjo, the declaration "will have a strong political impact."
He said Central America, rather than asking for direct, immediate free-trade negotiations with the United States, would propose steps toward closer trade and economic relations.

Several countries in the region, including Nicaragua and Guatemala, have expressed concerned that a new U.S. immigration law would harm them economically as they try to absorbe large numbers of deported illegal immigrants.
